notes_for_editor: Main narrative is built on the 2008 NPS Historic Structure Report (HSR; two-column PDF, so evidence quotes are line fragments) and NPS web pages; HSR cites letter-book indexes and Duffus's book The Lost Light that were not read directly. Disagreements flagged in the story: John R. Royal's first appointment (HSR: Jan 1834; USLHS and NPS list: 17 Jan 1854); third-order relighting (24 Feb vs 1 Mar 1863); raid date (3 vs 2 April 1864); kerosene (1873 NPS timeline vs late 1883 HSR); lens removal date (1975 vs undocumented); transfer to NPS (14 June HSR vs 14 July NPS timeline); incident when light went out (HSR text says 1875, cited index entries are Jan 1874); lens range (NPS pages say 15 and 18 miles). USLHS roster vs NPS list also differ on several tenures (Clifton to 1933 vs c.1930; Isaac V. Willis Jr. first assistant 1914-1933 on USLHS roster vs second assistant 1918-1920 on NPS list; NPS lists Josephus Willis 'May 21, 1869 until May 4, 1890', apparently a typo). The USLHS roster's 'James I. Davis' / 'James L. Davis' (NPS) / 'James S. Davis' (NPS Thurlow page) are likely one man but sources spell the initial differently. Roster lines carry person slugs from the USLHS record. The 'old lens' location rests on the HSR and the NPS beacons brochure; the NPS timeline says it went to the Portsmouth CG Support Center (an interim stop). The 1812 first-tower keeper description in the nomination is attributed to William Fulford (date of his remark unknown). The Today section reflects NPS updates through April 2026 and may be out of date; the stabilization was expected to take two to three years. No name-linking beyond the USLHS roster was done. Names of people active after 1960 are not used. Verifier note: the NPS timeline puts the IOV lamp in 1914 (with the occulting device) while the HSR and the NPS 1859 Lighthouse page say 1912; the story now states this.
